# Redirector domains REFUSED at create time (the `shorteners` feed seed).
# One domain per line; lines starting with # are comments.
#
# The test is whether the USER chose the shortener:
#
#   * General-purpose shorteners (below) are a deliberate choice. Shortening
#     an already-short link adds a hop for no benefit, it is the classic
#     laundering shape, and is.gd refuses the same thing. Refusing costs no
#     real traffic.
#   * Platform share wrappers are NOT refused: t.co, lnkd.in and buff.ly are
#     generated BY the platform when someone shares, so a user copying a
#     tweet or LinkedIn post link has one whether they wanted it or not.
#     Those are allowed and judged by where their chain actually ends.
#     Entries match every subdomain too, so a platform share subdomain of a
#     listed domain (maps.app.goo.gl) goes in redirector_domains.txt.
#
# Serving domains only, never corporate sites: bit.ly serves redirects,
# bitly.com hosts the product pages, so only bit.ly belongs here.
#
# Entries seed the feed ONCE, on first boot with an empty feed. After that
# the DB owns the set: operators (and the deep-analysis tier, for services
# it classifies as abuse-only) add entries live, and removals are never
# re-added from this file.

# general-purpose shorteners
bit.ly
